title: Help for first time directors: Training and resources from the Institute of Directors (IoD)
authors: Hugo Legh - Head of External Affairs, Institute of Directors

content.text: The Institute of Directors (IoD) supports directors and senior leaders in their careers. It provides practical guidance, professional development opportunities and resources to help you lead with confidence and impact.
Becoming a director is a significant career step, but it also brings new responsibilities. The IoD Boardroom Foundations and Code of Conduct resources can:
Understanding your role as a director

As a new director, you'll likely already have extensive senior experience. But taking on board-level responsibility is a different proposition from managing the day-to-day. You’ll need to understand your legal duties and governance obligations, balance the interests of your stakeholders and keep the long-term success of your organisation firmly in view.
Understanding this early will help you navigate complex decisions, ask the right questions and make an impact in the boardroom.
If you’re new to the boardroom – or are hoping to be appointed in the future – the IoD’s free Boardroom Essentials course gives you a solid grounding in what a director role realistically involves.

Knowing your responsibilities matters. But it's just as important to understand the standards you're expected to uphold. That’s where the IoD Code of Conduct for Directors comes in. It’s a practical framework for ethical, responsible leadership, setting out the principles you’ll need to demonstrate integrity, accountability and professionalism in the boardroom.
It’s a resource you’ll return to throughout your directorship, particularly when you’re weighing up your responsibilities or working through a difficult situation.
The benefits of continued professional development

Investing in your professional development brings benefits beyond growth on an individual level. As your knowledge, judgement and confidence develops, you’ll be better equipped to contribute effectively in the boardroom. It can support your organisation in strengthening its performance, make better decisions and create sustainable value.
That’s the Director Dividend: the personal and organisational return generated by more capable, informed and effective directors.
